question: Does the pinned SRA score implementation confuse integer target batch length B with class count C when B=C, violating batch partition, batch permutation, and class renaming invariance at fixed logits?
input_boundary: Only already-consumed development logits and manifest; no images, sealed confirmation/test data, checkpoints or training forward passes.
selection: All 589 development records, class count 37. Sort source IDs, then one fixed NumPy default_rng(20261023) permutation; take consecutive groups of 37, retaining the last group (34) as a negative control. No score-based selection.
primary_endpoint: Absolute difference between source-equivalent score on each hard-label batch and the published one-hot formula evaluated by an independent stable NumPy expression.
secondary_endpoints: Same rows evaluated in chunks of at most 18 (never C)
Same rows and labels permuted together, undo permutation afterward
Simultaneous random renaming of class indices and logit columns
Explicit one-hot input to the source formula
All rows evaluated together B=589 as a noncollision control
fairness: Logits, labels, sample identities, temperature=1 and score exponent 2/log(C) are fixed. Only batching / reversible index changes / equivalent label encoding vary. Fixed logits isolate this issue from BatchNorm and dropout.
stop_conditions: If fixed-score oracle mismatch does not exceed the preset numerical tolerance, do not claim the defect reproduced.
If noncollision, explicit one-hot or repaired-score controls fail, mark implementation verification invalid and diagnose rather than report success.
Stop at CPU wall cap 60 seconds per diagnostic invocation; at most one justified technical repair, no new scientific seeds.
Do not train to amplify an implementation edge case; do not claim original paper results invalid without an actual triggering batch in its protocol.
hypothesis_origin: Static source inspection before numeric execution. This is a reproducibility audit, not a preregistered generalization study or novel augmentation method.
screened_alternative: BatchNorm state touched by scoring is plausible, but Split BatchNorm prior work directly studies augmentation/normalization interplay; no new training is justified here.

access_events.action: List current processes to check competing training
Read recent normalization-state manuscript landing page

preservation: All pre-existing inputs/results read only. New outputs only in this newly created directory. No ARiS, PPT edits, other-project actions, uploads, sharing, remote writes, credentials, paid compute or Codex app operations.
